items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: They used to hear me practice but then they’d hear their uncle Alvin Batiste practice... Kent can hear how to play any kind of way.

ctx.x: Did the same thing go for your own children? Did they hear you practice?

They used to hear me practice but then they’d hear their uncle Alvin Batiste practice and it’s a funny thing about my kids. They never did — Kent can hear how to play any kind of way. But jazz is such a personal thing that the thing about jazz, there’s a whole lot of people want to play a certain way but they don’t have the motor skills to play a certain way. They don’t have the rhythmic thing in order to play a certain way. This is why I’ve seen people sit down and learn, I can listen to somebody play sometimes…

I couldn’t agree with you more. I mean you can’t teach a kid — you know it’s funny the first day, I should tell the people who are watching this that you’ve been doing a Louis Armstrong camp. And the first day I came down to watch a little bit and you were talking about tough love. And you said Kent knows about tough love. And then today when you were talking about, some of you guys were playing with your legs crossed, you’d better stop doing that or you’re going to be limping on the way home. Right?
